profile.name: Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library
profile.tagline: Inspiring leadership, conservation, and courageous citizenship through the life and legacy of Theodore Roosevelt.

items.headline: The Brownsville Affair: An Injustice That Took 66 Years to Correct
items.blurb: In 1906, soldiers of the all-Black 25th Infantry were wrongly accused after a Brownsville, Texas shooting, an injustice not corrected for 66 years.

items.headline: The Leadership of President Theodore Roosevelt with Robbie Lauf
items.blurb: How do you bring the legacy of America’s 26th president to life for a new generation in 2026?

items.headline: Theodore Roosevelt & Race: The Record and Its Contradictions
items.blurb: Roosevelt's writings, beliefs, and actions on race—full of contradictions—traced from the frontier world of his youth through his broader public…

items.headline: Peter Greenberg Worldwide — Medora, North Dakota - October 10, 2026 - Peter Greenberg…
items.blurb: This week’s broadcast of Peter Greenberg Worldwide is from the newly opened Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library in Medora, North Dakota.

items.headline: Theodore Roosevelt's Rise to Power
items.blurb: Trace Roosevelt's climb from Rough Rider to the White House — San Juan Hill, a vice presidency meant to sideline him, and the fateful autumn of 1901.

items.headline: The Assassination Attempt: Milwaukee, October 14, 1912
items.blurb: A delusional gunman shot Roosevelt in Milwaukee on October 14, 1912, an attempt that became one of the most dramatic moments of his campaign.

items.headline: The Coal Strike of 1902: The President Who Sided with the Miners
items.blurb: When 150,000 coal miners struck in 1902, Theodore Roosevelt intervened to end the crisis, marking a new role for the presidency in labor disputes.

items.headline: The Bull Moose Campaign of 1912: The Third-Party Insurgency
items.blurb: After breaking with President Taft over progressive reform, Roosevelt launched a bold third-party run in 1912 as the Bull Moose candidate.

items.headline: Theodore Roosevelt's Post-Presidency
items.blurb: Follow Roosevelt after the White House — a year-long African safari, the Bull Moose run of 1912, and a near-fatal plunge down Brazil's River of Doubt.

items.headline: Lessons learned from building the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library in the Badlands
items.blurb: The building is one of the first presidential libraries to pursue Living Building Challenge Certification, along with LEED Platinum and SITES…

items.headline: 51 Federal Bird Reserves: Roosevelt's Ornithological Vision
items.blurb: A boyhood love of birds led Theodore Roosevelt to establish 51 federal bird reserves, pioneering federal protection for America's wildlife.

items.headline: From White House Lenses to Local Wards: Pink at the Pump Live!
items.blurb: Broadcast live on location from PetroServe USA in Harwood, ND, Scott Hennon kicks off October's "Pink at the Pump" campaign, showing how everyday…

items.headline: Governor of New York: The Stepping Stone to the Presidency (1899-1900)
items.blurb: Riding fame from the Rough Riders and San Juan Hill, Theodore Roosevelt won the New York governorship in 1898, a key step toward the presidency.

items.headline: Bully, as Teddy Would Say: About Time for Roosevelt’s Presidential Library
items.blurb: The expansive history museum is in the Badlands, which made the man and made the president.

items.headline: The Roosevelt Family
items.blurb: Meet the Roosevelt family — TR's six spirited children, a family tree from New Amsterdam to two presidents, and the young niece named Eleanor.

items.headline: Theodore Roosevelt's Early Life
items.blurb: Meet the sickly, asthmatic boy of 28 East 20th Street who willed himself strong — Theodore Roosevelt's early years of grit, curiosity, and hard-won…

items.headline: Badlands Trails, Midterm Gambits, and the Fight for America’s Future (9-30-26)
items.blurb: Broadcast live from the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library in Medora, North Dakota, this packed episode covers local history, national politics…

items.headline: Theodore Roosevelt's Presidency
items.blurb: Step inside Roosevelt's presidency — the Square Deal, the Panama Canal, trust-busting, and a bully pulpit that redefined what the office could do.

items.headline: The River of Doubt: The Brazilian Expedition (1913
items.blurb: After his 1912 defeat, a restless Roosevelt joined a perilous expedition to map Brazil's uncharted River of Doubt deep in the Amazon.

items.headline: Kermit Roosevelt
items.blurb: The adventurous second son of Theodore and Edith, Kermit Roosevelt shared his father's love of exploration and the strenuous life.

items.headline: The Roosevelt White House: Renovation, Power, and Family Chaos
items.blurb: In 1902 Roosevelt hired McKim, Mead & White to modernize the White House and build the West Wing, all amid a house full of romping children.
